claims.hypothesis: A single migrating low-mass planet can produce the triple ring system with asymmetric separations
claims.experiment: 2D hydro plus RT of a 10 Earth-mass planet migrating from 69 to 64 au
claims.result: Model reproduces ring locations and fluxes of B2 and B3, B4 slightly brighter
claims.finding: Inward migration of a mini-Neptune explains the asymmetric separations

evidence.quote: a simple explanation, involving a single migrating low mass planet (10 M$_\oplus$), entirely accounts for such an apparently complex phenomenon.

claims.experiment: Ellipse fits to ring radii vs azimuth
claims.finding: All three outer rings have finite eccentricity

evidence.loc: 2.2 A triple ring system in the disk’s outer region

claims.hypothesis: An inner giant planet could create the outer rings
claims.result: Giant opens a gap but creates no additional narrow rings; induces eccentricity
claims.finding: Inner giant does not explain the triple ring

evidence.loc: 3.4.2 How does an inner giant planet impact the structure of rings B2, B3 and B4?
